## Current and recently submitted PhD students

::: {.student-entry #divya}

### Divya Tahelyani

**PhD thesis submitted, August 2026 · SRF, IIT Gandhinagar**

**Academic background.** MSc, Charotar University of Science and Technology.

Divya joined the PhD programme at IIT Gandhinagar in 2022 and submitted
her doctoral thesis in August 2026. She is currently continuing at IIT
Gandhinagar as a Senior Research Fellow.

Her research focuses on gravitational-wave astrophysics, including
multiband observations, decihertz gravitational-wave astronomy, and the
use of gravitational waves to probe dark-matter environments.

Recent work includes:

- [IndIGO-D: Probing Compact Binary Coalescences in the Decihertz GW Band](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06956)
- [Probing dark matter halo profiles with multiband observations of gravitational waves](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.14063)

[LinkedIn](https://in.linkedin.com/in/divya-tahelyani-00641515a)

:::

::: {.student-entry #ravi}

### Ravi Kesharwani

**Continuing Doctoral Programme (CDP) candidate, IIT Gandhinagar, 2026–present**

**Academic background.** Studied at VIIT Pune, 2011–2015.

Ravi is a Scientific/Technical Officer at IUCAA and works with the
LIGO-India instrumentation programme. He is also a member of the LIGO
Scientific Collaboration through IUCAA.

Before joining the LIGO instrumentation effort, Ravi worked on the
Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT) aboard the Aditya-L1 mission,
with a particular background in electro-optics and scientific
instrumentation.

He joined the Continuing Doctoral Programme (CDP) at IIT Gandhinagar in
January 2026. His doctoral work connects his experience in gravitational-wave
instrumentation with gravitational-wave physics.

## Former PhD students

::: {.student-entry #soumen}

### Soumen Roy

**PhD in Physics, IIT Gandhinagar, 2014–2020**

**Academic background.** MSc, University of Calcutta.

Soumen's doctoral research at IIT Gandhinagar focused on gravitational-wave
searches, template-bank construction, and the physics of compact-binary
inspirals.

After completing his PhD, he was a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at Nikhef,
Amsterdam, from December 2020 to August 2024. Since November 2024 he has
been a Postdoctoral Researcher at UCLouvain, Belgium.

**Post-IITGN research.** His subsequent work has included compact-binary
environments, tests of gravity with eccentric systems, and environmental
effects such as line-of-sight acceleration.

Representative work from his time at IIT Gandhinagar:

- [Unveiling the spectrum of inspiralling binary black holes](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.04565)
- [Effectual template banks for upcoming compact-binary searches in Advanced LIGO and Virgo data](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.08743)
- [Hybrid geometric-random template-placement algorithm for gravitational-wave searches](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.06771)

Selected later work:

- [Compact binary coalescences in dense gaseous environments can pose as ones in vacuum](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16388)
- [Testing modified gravity with the eccentric neutron star-black hole merger GW200105](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.21315)
- [Line-of-sight acceleration in compact binaries with higher harmonics and eccentricity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08838)

[LinkedIn](https://nl.linkedin.com/in/soumen-roy-6b388199)

:::

::: {.student-entry #amit}

### Amit Reza

**PhD in Computational Science, IIT Gandhinagar, 2014–2021**

**Academic background.** M.Tech., MANIT Bhopal.

Amit worked on computational methods for gravitational-wave searches,
including dimensionality reduction and efficient reconstruction of
matched-filter statistics.

He subsequently held a postdoctoral position at Nikhef and is currently
a Scientist at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in Graz.

**Post-IITGN research.** Amit has moved primarily into machine learning
for astrophysics and space science. His recent work includes neural-network
models for exoplanet atmospheres and climate, machine-learning classification
of space-debris light curves, and graph neural networks, alongside continued
connections with gravitational-wave data analysis.

[Current research profile](https://www.oeaw.ac.at/iwf/institut/das-team/exoplaneten-wetter-und-klima/reza-amit)

Representative work:

- [Random projections in gravitational-wave searches from compact binaries II](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.03226)
- [Fast likelihood evaluation using meshfree approximations for reconstructing compact binary sources](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02706)

[Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=TEpIWBcAAAAJ)

:::

::: {.student-entry #lalit}

### Lalit Pathak

**PhD, IIT Gandhinagar, 2018–2024**

**Academic background.** Department of Physics and Astrophysics, University of Delhi.

Lalit's doctoral work developed fast meshfree methods for gravitational-wave
parameter estimation and source localization. This included fast likelihood
evaluation, network sky localization, and interpolation of numerical-relativity
surrogate waveforms.

After IIT Gandhinagar he was at TIFR Mumbai during 2024–2025 and is
currently at IUCAA, Pune.

**Post-IITGN research.** Lalit has continued work on rapid
gravitational-wave inference while also moving into compact-binary
astrophysics. One recent direction concerns environmental effects on observed
signals, including line-of-sight acceleration from a possible tertiary
companion and its degeneracy with orbital eccentricity.

See
[On the Presence of a Tertiary Compact Object in GW190814](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21955).

Representative work:

- [Fast likelihood evaluation using meshfree approximations for reconstructing compact binary sources](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02706)
- [Prompt sky localization of compact binary sources using a meshfree approximation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07012)
- [Fast and faithful interpolation of numerical-relativity surrogate waveforms using a meshfree approximation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19162)

[Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=KhVSSlMAAAAJ&hl=en)

:::

::: {.student-entry #abhishek}

### Abhishek Sharma

**PhD, IIT Gandhinagar, 2021–2025**

**Academic background.** Jamia Millia Islamia; university gold medallist.

Abhishek worked on gravitational-wave inference across ground-based,
space-based, and decihertz detectors. His doctoral work included template
banks for non-standard compact-binary signals, accelerated parameter
estimation for LISA sources, and multiband gravitational-wave astronomy.

He is currently a postdoctoral researcher at IUCAA, Pune.

**Post-IITGN research.** Abhishek has continued developing fast
gravitational-wave inference methods while extending his work toward
space-based, decihertz, and multiband gravitational-wave astronomy.

Recent examples include
[Rapid parameter estimation with the full symphony of compact binary mergers using meshfree approximation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.04172)
and
[IndIGO-D: Probing Compact Binary Coalescences in the Decihertz GW Band](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06956).

Representative work:

- [Template bank to search for exotic gravitational-wave signals from astrophysical compact binaries](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03274)
- [Accelerated parameter estimation of supermassive black-hole binaries in LISA using a meshfree approximation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.14288)
- [IndIGO-D: Probing Compact Binary Coalescences in the Decihertz GW Band](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06956)

[LinkedIn](https://in.linkedin.com/in/abhishek-sharma-666a46205)
